task.description: WF-02 step 2c, security gate for REQ-001/REQ-007 (Pixel Office): a local server with a write secret, a hook that posts events, a page that reads a journal, and a project settings file that installs hooks. Review the implementation in tools/src/pixel-office/ (server.js, protocol.js, journal.js, state-dir.js, config.js, main.js, hook.sh, hook.js, public/*), .claude/settings.json and tools/README.md against the design's security model (§5 HTTP interface, §6 hook and settings, §7 security model, §8 error paths) and the quality bar Q7 (secrets by reference only), Q8 (n/a: no shop data — say so), Q9 (n/a, no SQL), Q10 (realistic failures never crash anything and hooks never break or slow a session), Q11 (external addresses: the server must be reachable only from the owner's own computer), R2 (only real hook events, no back-dated or hand-written events; list what a hostile local process or a web page in the owner's browser can and cannot do) and R3 (n/a). Test it, do not just read: start the real server code on a free port with a temp state directory (never port 4780, never ~/.sai-pixel-office) and try at least: wrong Host header and DNS-rebinding-style Host; a cross-origin web page reading the API and posting events; missing, wrong, replayed and stale HMAC signatures, a body signed for another path, oversized bodies (413), malformed JSON, unknown keys, header injection; path traversal and symlink tricks on the static routes; request smuggling basics; file modes of the state directory and secret (0700/0600) and what happens if they are wrong; the secret never in any response, log line, error message, README, settings file or client code (grep the repo); a hostile project path in settings.json (spaces, quotes, $(), backticks) and a hostile payload on hook stdin; the hook when the server is down, slow, or answers garbage (exit 0, silent, bounded time); a second server on the same port; stale port occupied by a foreign process; data minimisation (nothing from prompts, answers or file paths is stored or served); denial of service by a local process (journal growth, many connections). SAFETY: never start anything on port 4780 or with the real ~/.sai-pixel-office; do not start a real Claude Code session (it spends the owner's usage limit); never use a recursive chmod or follow symlinks when changing modes, and never create a symlink to a real binary (today a recursive chmod through a symlink broke the system Node); never write outside your scratchpad except your own handoff. Do not edit code. This shell has no `timeout`: bound every command.
acceptance_criteria: result.verdict PASS or FAIL against Q7, Q10, Q11, R2 (Q8, Q9, R3 stated not applicable)
each attack above tried with its result recorded (command and output in short)
findings located (file:line) with severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW) and concrete fix
statement what remains possible for a hostile local process (accepted residual risks of design §7.3) and whether they match the design
commands run listed; real ~/.sai-pixel-office and port 4780 untouched

result.summary: VERDICT: FAIL. One blocking defect (B1, quality-bar Q10 / [образец] INV-8): the Pixel Office server process dies on an unhandled EPIPE as soon as the reader of its stdout or stderr is gone. Nothing else I attacked broke the gate: no CRITICAL and no HIGH finding; Q7, Q11 and R2 pass; Q8, Q9 and R3 do not apply. The fix is two lines (below) and the re-check is short (scripts and a 6-line shell repro are kept, see RE-CHECK); I expect PASS after it. Per [образец]'s mandate there is no partial credit on an applicable invariant, so I do not pass it with a note. My verdict is not final on its own: the owner confirms the merge (R1). ITEMS ASSESSED (each one with the reason, as INV-6 requires) - Q7 secrets by reference only: PASS. The secret exists only in /write-secret (mode 0600, dir 0700, 32 random bytes = 43 base64url characters, created by open "wx" 0600). Greps over tools/src/pixel-office, .claude/settings.json, tools/README.md, tools/package.json, tools/eslint.config.js find no token-like string (a 40+ character [A-Za-z0-9_-] run exists only as comment rulers) and no password/token/api-key/bearer word; a grep of the whole sai/ tree (without node_modules) for a secret-word followed by 32+ characters finds nothing; the only key in the repo is the fictional "fictional-secret-AAAA..." of the design's probe P12. There is no client build: the bundle is public/ as served, so I fetched index, all 13 files of public/, /api/events and error answers from a running server: 17 responses, 0 occurrences of the real secret. Not in the server's stdout/stderr (several runs), not in argv or the environment listing (ps), not in error messages (a too-short secret file is reported by path only, the content was never printed). On the wire the hook sends only the signature: a foreign listener's capture shows no secret in headers or body and header = HMAC-SHA256(secret, exact body bytes). - Q8 (shop data separation): NOT APPLICABLE. Pixel Office holds no shop data; the journal has session/agent ids, role names and descriptions of at most 100 characters of the owner's own agent work. - Q9 (no SQL string building): NOT APPLICABLE. No database, no SQL: grep for select/insert/update-set/sqlite/postgres/mysql/.query( over tools/src/pixel-office and settings.json is empty. - Q10 (realistic failures never crash anything; hooks never break or slow a session): FAIL because of B1. Everything else under Q10 held: the hook always exits 0, silent, in at most 1.55 s (a 4 s limit is set in settings), over about 100 failure cases; the server survived about 43,000 fuzzed requests, floods, 3,000 idle connections, fd exhaustion, journal unwritable/unreadable/a directory/corrupt/truncated/deleted, and every other fault I injected. Two LOW defects touch Q10 (F1, F6). - Q11 (external addresses; server reachable only from the owner's computer): PASS. listen is server.listen(port, "127.0.0.1") (server.js:369); lsof -nP -iTCP: -sTCP:LISTEN shows only 127.0.0.1:; TCP connect to the LAN address 192.168.0.51 and to ::1 is refused; the Host check refuses 17 foreign or odd Host forms (see attack 1); no Access-Control-* header on any of 17 kinds of response; a real Chrome page could read nothing (attack 2); a second process cannot bind 127.0.0.1: while the server runs, also with SO_REUSEPORT (a wildcard 0.0.0.0 bind succeeds, but traffic to 127.0.0.1 still reaches the real server). The code makes no outbound request on behalf of anybody: the only two call sites are main.js:118 (probe, host is the constant 127.0.0.1, port is a checked integer) and hook.js:42 (host is the constant 127.0.0.1); the page fetch is a relative URL. There is no user-supplied URL, so the INV-9 style URL validation has nothing to validate. The hook does not follow redirects (a 302 to http://evil.example was not followed). - R2 (only real hook events, no back-dated or hand-written events): PASS. The only program path into events.jsonl is POST /api/events, and journal.append has a single caller (server.js:256). The order of checks is Host, size, signature, JSON, key allow-list, then the time check and the append in one synchronous sequence (no await between them). source is put in by the server and refused in a request (has_source for REAL, SIMULATION and empty). The hook stamps the time as its first statement. A write more than 60 s away from the server clock is refused (+-61 s, 1 h, 1 day, 1 year: 400 time_skew, journal unchanged). No seed/demo/simulation/back-fill code exists anywhere in tools/src/pixel-office (grep). The page marks foreign lines (my run of model.js: source not REAL -> marked, line dated 1 h before the last honest line -> marked "conflict", future-dated last line -> marked "future"). Limits that the design already accepts are listed under RESIDUAL RISKS; the one new item is replay (F2, LOW). - R3 (customer photos): NOT APPLICABLE. No photos, no customer data; nothing of the kind is stored, logged or served. BLOCKING FINDING B1 MEDIUM (blocks: Q10 / INV-8). The server dies on an unhandled EPIPE when the reader of its stdout or stderr has gone. Where: tools/src/pixel-office/main.js:296-307 (the entry point installs no 'error' listener on process.stdout or process.stderr); the sinks are server.js:116-122 (warn: only a synchronous throw is caught; the comment says "A failing warning sink must not stop the server"), journal.js:86-88 (defaultWarn) and the link line main.js:247. Repro, plain shell (kept in the scratchpad as the commands of this step): D=$(mktemp -d); mkdir -p $D/home $D/state; chmod 700 $D/state; ( HOME=$D/home SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR=$D/state node tools/src/pixel-office/main.js --dir $D/state --port 0 2>&1 | head -n 1 > $D/link ) & (head exits after the link line, like a tee, a harness pipe or a closed pipe) ; then curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:/$(printf 'a%.0s' $(seq 300)).js -> 500, and the server is gone: the next request gets "connection refused". An observer-only preload shows the cause: uncaughtException EPIPE write, exit code 1. Any warning does it (a 500 in a handler, a corrupt journal line - tried, a failed append, a read failure), so any local process can trigger it with one request once the pipe is closed. Second form: if the reader of stdout is already gone when the link line is printed, the server dies right after start with a raw Node stack ("Unhandled 'error' event ... Error: write EPIPE"), which also contradicts design E25 (no stack trace). Why this is a Q10 failure: it is a process crash on an I/O error of its own output channel, reachable from network input, in the same class as AP-014 ("fix the class, not the named places": OS errors; the class list of the design names fs, net, http, child_process, crypto and misses the stdio streams). The design's UAT recipe starts the server "in the background, output to a file" (design 10.4 a), which is safe; but README and section 9.3 do not say how ORCH starts it, and a pipe that closes after launch is the common way agents start background servers. Fix (verified from outside the repo: a preload that does only this made the same repro survive 3 long-name requests and a corrupt-journal warning, final GET 200): in main.js, before main() runs in the entry-point block: for (const s of [process.stdout, process.stderr]) s.on("error", () => {}); This covers server.js, journal.js and main.js writes. Tests to add (TEST-DESIGNER): (1) spawn main.js with piped stdio, destroy the child's stderr reader, request '/' + 'a'*300 + '.js', assert the process is alive and GET /api/events?after=0&limit=0 answers 200; (2) the same with stdout closed before the link line: alive, SIGTERM gives exit 0, no "Unhandled 'error' event" on stderr. OTHER FINDINGS (none blocks; I recommend F1, F2, F3 and F6 in the same pass as B1, because they are one-liners) F1 LOW (Q10). GET /<256 or more characters>.js answers 500 {"error":"internal"} and writes a stderr line with the absolute repo path, instead of 404 (design 5.2: names that do not fit -> 404). server.js:56 (STATIC_NAME has no length bound) and server.js:158-163 (only ENOENT, EISDIR, ENOTDIR map to 404; ENAMETOOLONG falls through). In the fuzz run this is the only 5xx shape (78 of 43,200 requests). It is also the cheapest trigger for B1. Fix: STATIC_NAME = /^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$/ and add ENAMETOOLONG and ELOOP to the 404 list. Test: extend SV-36 with '/' + 'a'*300 + '.js' -> 404 and empty stderr. F2 LOW (R2). Replay. A captured (body, signature) pair is accepted again and again inside the +-60 s window and each time appends a line (3 sends -> +3 lines; replay after the window -> 400 time_skew; the foreign-listener capture was accepted twice by the real server). It needs someone who saw a signed request: a foreign process on a stale port (design T6) or the secret holder. A replayed SubagentStart after the matching SubagentStop within 60 s would reopen a task on the page. Where: server.js:228-264, protocol.js:119-128. Fix: remember the signatures of accepted bodies for 120 s (a Map pruned by time) and answer a repeat with 204 without appending. Test: same (body, signature) twice -> journal +1. F3 LOW. Symlinks are followed in four places. Precondition in every case: write access to the 0700 state dir or to the repo, i.e. the owner or an owner-level process, so no new capability; I list it because it is the class of today's chmod-through-symlink incident. (a) state-dir.js:181-208 readExistingSecret: statSync and chmodSync(file, 0600) follow a symlinked write-secret; observed with a symlink to a scratch text file: the target's mode went 0644 -> 0600 and its content became the secret. (b) state-dir.js:232-240 writeSmallFile: writeFileSync and chmodSync on .tmp- follow a pre-planted symlink (read from code, not exercised: needs the pid). (c) journal.js:56 openSync(file, "a+") follows a symlinked events.jsonl; observed: lines went to the target. (d) server.js:157 readFileSync(public/) follows a symlink inside public/; observed: a file outside public/ was served with 200 (design T8 only claims a flat directory and three extensions). Fix: lstat first and refuse non-regular files; open with fs.constants.O_NOFOLLOW; fchmodSync(fd) instead of chmodSync(path); create the temp file with flag "wx" after rmSync(tmp, {force: true}); static files: lstatSync(...).isFile() before reading. Tests: symlinked write-secret and events.jsonl -> clear message, target untouched (the link target of such a test must be a scratch text file, never a binary). F4 LOW (R2; a gap in design T6). The start probe trusts any JSON with "app":"sai-pixel-office" (main.js:104-158, check at 141-145). A process that binds the free port before the server starts (any local account can) and imitates that answer makes `npm run pixel-office` print the link and exit 0 (observed: exit 0 in 84 ms), so the owner would look at a forged page. A squatter that does not imitate the marker is detected (9 kinds of occupant tried, see attack 12). Fix (optional): challenge-response: the probe sends ?nonce=, the server answers HMAC(secret, nonce), main.js checks it with the secret it already read; or write it into README as a known limit. F5 LOW. A web page in the owner's browser can make the server work: cross-site requests are processed (in the Chrome run every request of the hostile page reached the server with sec-fetch-site: cross-site and, for most, an Origin header of the hostile page, and was processed: GET 200, POST 401, OPTIONS 405; GET ?after=0 reads the whole journal). Nothing is readable or writable (attack 2), but with a big journal a page can keep the event loop busy and make hook POSTs time out (F7). Where: server.js:300-330 (route has no Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site check). Fix: answer 403 before the journal is touched when Sec-Fetch-Site is cross-site or same-site, or when an Origin header is present and is not http://127.0.0.1: or http://localhost:; add Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin. Tests in the style of SV-22. F6 LOW. server.js:222 answerTooLarge calls socket.setTimeout(ms, callback) on every 413, and each call adds one 'timeout' listener. 40 oversized requests on one keep-alive connection give "MaxListenersExceededWarning: 11 timeout listeners" on stderr (no crash, no leak beyond the socket's life; all 40 got their 413). Fix: arm once per socket (a WeakSet) or call setTimeout(ms) once and use a single once('timeout'). F7 LOW (the README states the page limit, limit 13, but not the server consequence). GET /api/events?after=0 has no cap. Measured: 100,000 lines (27 MB) 223 ms and +260 MB RSS; 300,000 lines (80 MB) 656 ms and 901 MB RSS; while three full GETs of 300,000 lines run, a tiny GET waited 1,754 ms (a hook POST arriving then would hit its 1 s limit and its event is lost). The heap limit here is 4,144 MB, so a full GET should run out of memory (fatal, not catchable) at roughly 1.4 million lines (extrapolated from the two measurements, NOT run). A holder of the secret writes 15,233 lines/s (4,000 in 0.3 s, 105 bytes per line), so 700,000 lines take under a minute; organic growth to that size takes years; an unauthorised process cannot grow the journal at all (0 lines after 20,000 unsigned POSTs). Where: server.js:176-214, journal.js:293-311 (readLines allocates the whole range). Fix: cap `events` per response (for example 50,000); the page already continues from entries.length. F8 LOW (conditional; impact high if it happens). .claude/settings.json:7-16 and the six identical handlers: the handler is command "/bin/sh" plus args. A Claude Code that ignored args would run a bare /bin/sh with the hook JSON on stdin as the script. I checked what that does: a bare /bin/sh executed the $(...) and backtick text inside such a JSON line (a harmless touch in a scratch directory ran). The docs describe the exec form (WebFetch of code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks: "no shell, each args element is one argument exactly as written") and all 10 Claude Code extension binaries installed here (2.1.263-2.1.286) contain the exec-form schema text, so the owner's installs are covered; the first version that has args is not stated in the docs or the changelog I could fetch. Fix: state the minimum version in README (2.1.263 is the oldest installed), or (needs a probe) use a shell-form command that reads the environment variable "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" inside double quotes (design probe P1 shows it is in the hook environment): safe for hostile paths and for versions without args. F9 INFO. hook.sh:17: the read of node-path blocks for ever when node-path is a FIFO (only Claude Code's timeout 4 ends it; precondition: write access to the state dir). Fix: [ -f "$dir/node-path" ] before the read. F10 INFO. server.js:303-310: with two Host headers the first wins (good then evil -> 200; evil then good -> 403). RFC 9112 wants 400; a browser cannot send two. Fix: count the Host entries in req.rawHeaders. F11 INFO. journal.js:56 does not narrow a pre-existing events.jsonl or server-starts.jsonl (observed: 0644 kept inside the narrowed 0700 dir, so no exposure). state-dir.js:90-99: SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR or --dir pointing at a populated directory (for example $HOME) gets that directory chmod 0700 and the five files. Fix: fchmod after open; mention it in README. F12 INFO (process). Nothing forbids agents from editing .claude/settings.json, and design test ST-01 checks the shape of the handlers but not their text, so an edit that adds a command to the guard would still pass ST-01. Proposal: pin the whole handler JSON in ST-01 and add a mandate line. F13 INFO. A backslash in a directory name of the project path makes Node fail to import the siblings of hook.js (28 single special characters tried, only the backslash breaks it); the hook then exits 0 silently, so events are lost without a message (Q10 holds). <папка Sai> has none. ATTACKS TRIED AND RESULTS (real main.js or real server.js on port 0 in a temp state dir with HOME in a temp dir; scripts t1..t16 and logs t*.out in the scratchpad, see COMMANDS) 1. Wrong Host and DNS rebinding (t1, t7). 17 foreign or odd Host values on GET (evil.example, evil.example:, other port, localhost without port, 127.0.0.1 without port, empty, 0.0.0.0:, [::1]:, LOCALHOST:, localhost.:, 127.0.0.1.:, "good, evil", good@evil, evil#@good, 2130706433:, 127.1:, 0x7f.0.0.1:) -> all 403 with an empty body; the 3 good forms (127.0.0.1: with and without a trailing space, localhost:) -> 200. No Host: HTTP/1.1 -> 400 (Node itself), HTTP/1.0 -> 403. Two Host headers: first wins (F10). Absolute-URI target with a good Host -> 404, with an evil Host -> 403. X-Forwarded-Host and Forwarded are ignored. A correctly signed POST with 4 wrong Host values -> 403 and the journal is unchanged. In Chrome the rebinding end state (Host evil.test:) got 403 twice. 2. Cross-origin page in a real browser (t7; Chrome 154.0.8037.59 headless, throwaway profile; the hostile page was served from http://evil.test:, a name mapped to loopback inside that browser only, which is the worst case because no Private/Local Network Access check applies; a request logger around the real server code shows what arrived). 14 attempts, 0 readable: CORS GET of the journal blocked (Failed to fetch); no-cors GET reached the server (200) and stayed opaque; JSON POST needed a preflight, OPTIONS got 405 and the POST was never sent; text/plain POST and a text/plain form POST in a hidden iframe reached the server and got 401 (3 POSTs, all 401); script include of the API blocked (nosniff, not JavaScript); iframe of the page: DOM unreadable (X-Frame-Options DENY and frame-ancestors 'none' are on the HTML); WebSocket and EventSource refused; of the API is not an image; CORS GET of app.js blocked. The journal was unchanged and the forged session text absent. What the page can still do is F5 (blind requests). 3. HMAC (t2, t2b). Missing, wrong (zeros, random), signature of another body, other 43-character secret, key = decoded secret bytes, empty key, 8 malformed forms (empty, 63 or 65 hex, non-hex, 0x prefix, leading space, two joined by a comma, base64), duplicate signature headers in both orders, the secret itself in Authorization: Bearer and in a custom header -> all 401, journal unchanged. A valid MAC is also accepted with an upper-case header name, upper-case hex, and a trailing space (the HTTP parser trims it) -> 204. Stale and future: +-59.5 s -> 204; +-61 s, +-1 h, +-1 day, +-1 year -> 400 time_skew. Replay: F2. A body signed together with another path -> 401; a valid signature POSTed to /api/other or /api/events/ -> 404; PUT -> 405; a query string is accepted (not part of the MAC). The MAC covers the body only; with one write endpoint nothing can be cross-used; if a second signed endpoint is ever added, the path must go into the MAC input. 4. Bodies, JSON, keys (t2). 413 for 16,385 / 20,000 / 1 MiB (signed or not) and for a 40,000-byte chunked body; exactly 16,384 bytes -> 204; Content-Length 99999999999999999999 and -5 -> 400; a client that declared 100,000 bytes and sent 100 got the 413 at once and was dropped by the 5 s timer. 33 signed body cases: not JSON, empty, array, null, number, string, BOM, {}, unknown event, unknown keys (prompt, cwd, transcript_path, a key made of markup -> "unknown_key:?"), source REAL / SIMULATION / empty -> has_source, __proto__ and constructor keys, 129-character ids, wrong types, bad times, missing required keys -> 400 with the matching reason; error bodies repeat nothing of the request; duplicate JSON keys -> 204 (last wins, still allow-listed). 5. Header injection and smuggling basics (t2). %0d%0a in the path or query -> no injected header or body; raw bare LF, lone CR, NUL, space before the colon, obs-fold -> 400; 20 KiB header, 10,000 headers, 20 KiB URL -> 431; Content-Length with Transfer-Encoding (both orders), two different Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding xchunked, "chunked, identity", a leading-space Transfer-Encoding, Content-Length +N and 0xN -> 400 (Node's parser); a legal chunk extension -> 204; pipelined [unsigned POST, GET, GET with evil Host, GET /] -> 401, 200, 403, 200, each judged on its own; a body shaped like a GET request is not executed (exactly one 401). 6. Static routes and path traversal (t1, t4). 53 paths (.., %2e%2e, %2f, //, backslash, NUL, %00, %2500, dotfiles, subpaths, other extensions, hook.js/config.js/server.js/main.js/journal.js/state-dir.js/protocol.js, write-secret/events.jsonl/server-starts.jsonl/port/node-path, /public/app.js, case changes) -> 404; a query like ?../../etc/passwd is ignored; every file of public/ by name -> 200 (13 files); a directory named x.js -> 404; symlinks inside public/: F3(d); 256+ character names: F1. 7. State directory modes and what happens when they are wrong (t4). Normal start: dir 0700, five files 0600, no *.tmp-* left. Wrong: dir 0777 -> narrowed to 0700; secret 0644 -> 0600 with the same secret kept; port and node-path 0644 -> rewritten as 0600; a pre-existing events.jsonl 0644 stays (F11); dir 0000 -> server starts, dir becomes 0700; state path is a file or a symlink to a directory -> exit 1 with a clear message, nothing created inside the link target; a deep path is created with 0700 at every level; secret shorter than 43 -> exit 1, file unchanged, content not printed; secret path a directory or 5,000 bytes -> exit 1; relative --dir -> exit 2, relative SAI_PIXEL_OFFICE_DIR -> exit 1; symlinked write-secret or events.jsonl: F3(a), F3(c). Not testable here: another OS account owning the directory (state-dir.js:84), the machine has one user. 8. Secret nowhere (t1, t3, t4, t8; greps). See Q7. Also the secret is not in the 401/400/403/413/500 bodies and not in ps argv or the environment listing of the running server. 9. settings.json and a hostile project path (t3, t3b, t3c). Structure: the only top-level key is hooks; exactly the 7 events; matcher Agent only on PostToolUse; every handler is type command, /bin/sh with args [-c, guard, sai-pixel-office, ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}], timeout 4, no async; one identical guard; no URL, token, env, permissions or mcp keys. Only sai/.claude/settings.json defines hooks (find over ~/.claude and <общая папка>: the other three settings files have no hooks key). The guard was run as /bin/sh -c sai-pixel-office against the real hook files of the repo and against copies placed in directories named: 'evil dir $(touch PWN1) `touch PWN2` 'q' "d" ;touch PWN3; &&touch PWN4 #x', a name with a newline and $(), '-rf', 'a b', plus an empty path, an unsubstituted ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}, a nonexistent dir and a dir without hook files: always exit 0, stdout empty, stderr exactly "sai-pixel-office", no PWN file anywhere, and the event is written where hook files exist. 28 single special characters in a directory name: all work except the backslash (F13). The substitution of ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR} by Claude Code itself could not be run (no real session, by instruction): the docs state each args element is passed as one plain string with no shell, and the design's probes P1 and P3 ran it. 10. Hostile hook stdin (t3, t3c, t14). 27 payloads: empty, whitespace, not JSON, null, array, NUL bytes, invalid UTF-8, shell metacharacters ($(), backticks, ;, &&, |) in forbidden fields and in allowed fields, markup, quotes, RTL and NUL in the description, __proto__ and constructor keys, unknown event, wrong case, ids of 129 characters and 1 MiB, a non-Agent tool, no agentId, wrong types, 7 MiB and 9 MiB input, 200,000-level nested arrays, 300,000 keys, emoji, a lone surrogate: always exit 0, stdout empty, stderr only the label, at most 150 ms. Stored lines hold only allowed keys and none of the dropped texts (prompt, cwd, transcript_path, last_assistant_message, session_title, task prompt); metacharacters in allowed fields are stored as literal text and nothing runs; descriptions are cut to 100 code points. 9 worst-case inputs of exactly 8 MiB (nested arrays and objects, 700,000 keys, long strings): at most 524 ms. 11. Hook when the server is down, slow or answers garbage (t3, t15). Server down 75 ms; accepts and stays silent 1,081 ms; garbage and close 88 ms; 200 then an endless trickle 1,080 ms; accept queue full (connect never completes) 1,108 ms; 302 to http://evil.example not followed; 400/401/403/413/500 71 ms; a 50 MB answer 151 ms; stdin never closed 1,552 ms (hard exit); port file missing, garbage, 99999, 0, -1, "80 80", a directory, 1 MiB; secret missing, empty, short, 1 MiB, a directory; state dir missing; HOME unset; relative dir; no Node 22 (a v25 stub, or none); node-path pointing at a missing file, a directory, a non-executable file, binary garbage, or a script that prints noise and exits 7: all exit 0 with empty stdout and only the label on stderr, at most 85 ms except the bounded cases above and one 567 ms case (a Node 25 stub on PATH, no node-path, no fallbacks); hook.sh run directly: stdout and stderr empty.
